Hasan Foez Siddique J: These Criminal Petitions for Leave to Appeal Nos. 663, 693-98, 614,621,633-34,665,667-70 of 2014 and 11-13 of 2015 have been heard together and they are being disposed of by this common judgment and order since facts of all the cases and law related thereto are identical.  44. The learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners of all the petitions, submit that strong prima-facie arguable case have been established against the accused respondents in all the cases and accordingly the learned Divisional Special Judge, Chittagong took cognizance against them, the High Court Division committed an error of law in quashing the proceeding. They submit that the time stipulated for concluding investigation in the law is not mandatory in nature since there is no penal provision in the relevant law. They submits that in all cases there were certifications that the works had been completed satisfactorily as to the specification provided in the schedules of contracts and there were also certification in all cases that billed amounts were not more than the value of the works actually done. In view of such certifications, there were no scope to deduct the amount withdrawn, so there were no illegality in the initiations of the impugned proceedings. 

 46. In the instant cases, it appears from the FIR and the Police reports that prima-facie arguable case had been made out against the accused respondents. The High Court Division, in fact, quashed the proceeding relying upon the case of the State vs Lailun Nahar Ekram reported in IV ADC 264. In the cited case this Division observed that after completion of entire work of the project when the final bill would be submitted, the authority (IPSA) would be at liberty to adjust deduct any excess amount if paid to the respondent in making payment against running bills. Facts and circumstances of the cited case and these cases are distinguishable. In all the cases it had been certified that the billed amounts are not more than the value of the works actually done. It is relevant here to quote some portions of the report of Investigating Officer. In PS Case No. 14 dated 5-9-2010 corresponding to ACC GR Case No. 23 of 2010 the Investigating Officer has stated that, "অথচ উক্ত ৩টি চলতি বিল প্রদান কালে বর্ণিত কৌশলীগণ এই মর্মে প্রত্যায়ন করে যে,"the works have been done satisfactorily and accordingly to the specification as per schedule of contract. Further certified that the billed amount is not more than the value of work actually done" 

 On perusal of the charge-sheets of all the cases it appears that such observations of the Investigating Officer are common. In such view of the facts, circumstances and material on records, particularly, the conclusions arrived at by the Investigating Officer, quoted above, the view expressed by this Division in above cited case is not applicable in these cases. 

 47. Another ground for quashing the proceedings by the High Court Division is that though the Chief Engineer and Superintending Engineer approved the bills they had not been implicated as accused so the proceedings against the accused respondents are bad in law. Non implicating any person as accused in a proceeding cannot be a ground for quashing the proceeding of the charge-sheeted accused when the prima-facie case had been established against him. 

 50. From the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the cases, we are of the view that it would be unnecessary delay in holding the trial of the cases, if we grant leaves. 

 51. The judgment and order dated 24-4-2014 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 20624, 20629, 20630, 20632, 20633, 20639, 20641,20625, 20627, 21412, 21413, 20637, 20626, 20636, 20634, 20638,20635,20631, and 20628 of 2013 passed by the High Court Division are hereby set aside. The Divisional Special Judge, Chittagong is directed to proceed with the cases in accordance with law.
